milestones.label: Artificial general intelligence
milestones.definition: Reliable, adaptable intelligence at skilled human level across a representative range of unfamiliar cognitive tasks.

criteria.label: Breadth at skilled human level
criteria.rule: On a preregistered, representative battery spanning reasoning, language, quantitative work and practical problem solving, the same system reaches the skilled-human comparison group in each domain. Use the lower uncertainty bound of its paired performance difference and a published equivalence margin.

criteria.label: Transfer to unfamiliar tasks
criteria.rule: An independent evaluation finds skilled-human performance on held-out task families, with an audit for training overlap, fixed resource limits and no task-specific retraining.

criteria.label: Reliability across settings
criteria.rule: Independent evaluators repeat the breadth and transfer findings on fresh cases and task variants with the same system and disclosed assistance. They report failures and uncertainty.

milestones.limitations: Unmeasured or conflicting criteria leave the total indeterminate. Related benchmarks describe narrower abilities.

milestones.label: Recursive self-improvement
milestones.definition: Repeatable cycles in which an AI materially improves a successor that itself contributes to further improvements.

criteria.label: A material contribution to a successor
criteria.rule: A controlled comparison attributes a reproducible gain in a named successor to its predecessor’s research, holding other inputs fixed or estimating their effects. Evaluate the gain on independent held-out tasks.

criteria.label: Repeated improvement by successors
criteria.rule: The improved successor itself contributes a material independently verified improvement to the next generation in the same lineage. Publish protocols and evidence for both links.

milestones.limitations: Unmeasured or conflicting criteria leave the total indeterminate. Related benchmarks describe narrower abilities.

milestones.label: Artificial superintelligence
milestones.definition: Reliable capabilities substantially exceeding leading human experts across a broad range of cognitive domains. Under this definition it also satisfies AGI.

criteria.label: Breadth at skilled human level
criteria.rule: On a preregistered, representative battery spanning reasoning, language, quantitative work and practical problem solving, the same system reaches the skilled-human comparison group in each domain. Use the lower uncertainty bound of its paired performance difference and a published equivalence margin.

criteria.label: Transfer to unfamiliar tasks
criteria.rule: An independent evaluation finds skilled-human performance on held-out task families, with an audit for training overlap, fixed resource limits and no task-specific retraining.

criteria.label: Reliability across settings
criteria.rule: Independent evaluators repeat the breadth and transfer findings on fresh cases and task variants with the same system and disclosed assistance. They report failures and uncertainty.

criteria.label: Broad expert superiority
criteria.rule: On that same cross-domain battery, the system repeatedly exceeds leading experts by a practically meaningful preregistered margin in each domain. Independent replications must support the lower bound of the difference.

milestones.limitations: Unmeasured or conflicting criteria leave the total indeterminate. Related benchmarks describe narrower abilities.

milestones.label: Technological singularity
milestones.definition: A sustained transition in which AI-driven feedback accelerates technological improvement across successive generations and changes its established rate.

criteria.label: Self-reinforcing research
criteria.rule: Independent evidence identifies successive generations carrying their improvements into further research, with repeatable gains attributable to their work.

criteria.label: Sustained acceleration
criteria.rule: At least three successive development intervals allow two successive increases in the comparable rate of capability gain. Uncertainty bounds and alternative explanations, including spending, compute and staffing, must be addressed.

criteria.label: A change in technological progress
criteria.rule: Independent replication across development settings demonstrates a sustained break from the preceding rate of technological progress, attributable to that feedback. Report comparable pre-transition and post-transition measurements.

milestones.limitations: Unmeasured or conflicting criteria leave the total indeterminate. Related benchmarks describe narrower abilities.

sources.title: AI Impacts · Survey of machine-learning researchers
sources.finding: The survey obtained 1,580 valid responses. Its combined forecasts put a 10% chance on machines doing every task better and more cheaply by 2027 and 50% by 2042. The halfway year was 2036 for doing research and writing a machine-learning conference paper, and 2052 for automating the occupation of AI researcher.
sources.limitation: Respondents answered subsets of questions and assumed no major disruption to science. Conditional on human-level machines, median respondents assigned 10% within two years and 60% within thirty years to vastly superhuman performance across professions. For a dramatic AI-driven acceleration of global technology, those figures were 20% and 80%. The Watch requires independent tests and evidence of a repeating causal loop.
sources.locator: Sections 2.3 and 3.2, Table 2, and Appendices E and F

sources.title: Forecasting Research Institute · Longitudinal Expert AI Panel, wave 8
sources.finding: The median expert gave an 80% chance of majority panel agreement on expert-level AGI before 2100. Given that recognition, the quarter, halfway and three-quarter dates were 2039, 2050 and 2065. A separate question on recognizing rapid progress gave 68% before 2100 and a conditional halfway year of 2045.
sources.limitation: The AGI question requires a commercial system that beats 90th-percentile professionals on at least 90% of nonphysical tasks in every primarily nonphysical occupation, at up to five times the equivalent labor cost. Its rapid-progress scenario also involves physical capabilities. Neither question stipulates the Watch’s testing or causal rules.

sources.title: Metaculus · When will a general AI system be publicly announced?
sources.finding: On November 24, the community forecast centered on 2030 for the first general AI system to be built, tested and publicly announced under the question’s rules.
sources.limitation: This crowd forecast can change as people update their predictions. Its public announcement date offers a comparison with the Watch’s estimate for independently demonstrated ability across domains. It has no weight in the Watch’s calculation.

sources.title: AI Futures Project · November timelines update
sources.finding: All six authors placed their halfway date for a superhuman AI researcher in 2027. Five placed the date for AI that outperforms top experts across virtually all cognitive tasks in 2028 and one in 2027.
sources.limitation: The authors assume no substantial deliberate slowdown and draw heavily on the same METR report about Anthropic. Their research milestone requires automated coding and experiment selection on par with the best human researcher. It can be reached before anyone independently verifies a repeating successor lineage.

sources.title: Forecasting Research Institute · Measuring a year of unusually fast gains
sources.finding: The researchers modeled a rise of at least 30 points in the best Epoch Capabilities Index score within twelve months. Their statistical model put its chance at 12% by the end of 2027 and 38% by the end of 2030.
sources.limitation: Under other plausible assumptions about volatility, their 2030 figure ranged from 7% to 59%. One year of gains on an index leaves the cause, persistence across generations and effect on technology beyond AI open.
sources.locator: Section 2.3 and its second endnote, November 2026 revision

sources.title: Forecasting Research Institute · Economic growth under rapid AI progress
sources.finding: Even assuming rapid AI progress, the expert panel’s median forecast for annual growth in advanced economies in 2050 was 5%, against a roughly 2% historical pace. The median among tournament forecasters was 3%.
sources.limitation: Economic output reflects financing, adoption, physical production and regional conditions. A jump in research capability can take years to reach these measures. GDP growth alone cannot identify a repeating improvement cycle or its cause.

sources.title: METR · AI research and development at Anthropic
sources.finding: At Anthropic, measured gains on the lab’s capability index came 1.9 times as fast after October 2025 as in the earlier period. The reported 95% interval was 1.5–2.8 times. METR judged that AI probably accounted for most of the recent acceleration.
sources.limitation: The attribution is a judgment under substantial uncertainty. Staff changes, compute, the choice of tasks and the earlier growth rate can also affect this one lab’s comparison.

sources.title: METR · Duration of AI tasks in the Q4 capability evaluation
sources.finding: Across two task suites, METR estimated that the human-expert working time corresponding to 50% AI success doubled every 3.61 months. The 95% interval on the doubling time was 2.08–4.94 months.
sources.limitation: These tasks emphasize software and research work. Longer tasks, higher reliability, transfer to unfamiliar domains and open-ended research each need their own measurements.

sources.title: Sakana AI and UBC · Darwin Gödel Machine
sources.finding: Researchers reported a coding agent that repeatedly edited agent code and tested successors. The resulting system’s SWE-bench score rose from 20% to 50%, with a separate coding benchmark improving from 14.2% to 30.7%.
sources.limitation: This developer experiment changed the software around a foundation model. A public, independently verified lineage would need to connect specific successive changes to the Watch’s required capability gains.

sources.title: Wang and colleagues · Testing self-improving coding agents
sources.finding: A second team reran the Darwin Gödel Machine method with different underlying models and a common starting agent. The starting agent solved 40% of a 60-task software test. Its selected successor scored 53.3%.
sources.limitation: This independently tests whether the method can discover better coding agents. The initial-to-final comparison does not identify how much each of two successive generations contributed on independent held-out tasks.

sources.title: ARC Prize · GPT-6.2 Astra on interactive reasoning tasks
sources.finding: On ARC-AGI-3, GPT-6.2 Astra at the same maximum reasoning setting scored 70.3% with the standard setup and 99.8% with the provider’s adapter, which retains the model’s internal reasoning state between requests.
sources.limitation: The tested setup matters even for the same model. The score describes a specific collection of interactive puzzles. Evidence from other domains and independent tests of transfer are still needed.

sources.title: Epoch AI · Attribution of solutions to open mathematics problems
sources.finding: Of 49 open mathematical challenges in the register on November 24, Epoch credited five solutions to AI alone and five to people working with AI. The distinction records who contributed the ideas behind each solution.
sources.limitation: A solution establishes a particular mathematical result. Judging broad superiority to leading experts requires repeatable comparisons across multiple disciplines.

sources.title: Epoch AI · Can AI automate Epoch?
sources.finding: Epoch gave six models tasks drawn from its own work. Stronger systems could suggest research directions but struggled to design experiments that would resolve the question or to catch flaws in their own experimental setup.
sources.limitation: The evaluators used one organization’s tasks and quality standards. The experiment identifies practical gaps without establishing a universal ceiling.

observatoryObservations.label: Mathematical reasoning on AIME 2024
observatoryObservations.summary: The authors report that performance rose from 15.6% to 77.9% during reinforcement learning.
observatoryObservations.limitations: One mathematics contest and one training procedure. Peer review does not provide an independent replication on unfamiliar domains.

observatoryObservations.label: Strategy in multiplayer Diplomacy
observatoryObservations.summary: In its August–October 2022 study, CICERO placed in the top tenth of human participants who played more than once.
observatoryObservations.limitations: Repeated play within a single structured game. This test cannot establish strategic ability in other settings or intent in deployment.

observatoryObservations.measurementDateBasis: End of the reported driving period
observatoryObservations.label: Rider-only distance observed
observatoryObservations.source: Kusano and colleagues, Traffic Injury Prevention
observatoryObservations.limitations: The authors work for Waymo. Distance in the service’s operational domain measures exposure. Other environments, tasks and human support practices need separate evaluation.

observatoryObservations.label: An AI-discovered improvement to model training
observatoryObservations.limitations: A reported training-kernel improvement. It does not demonstrate a capability increase in a named successor or a repeated improvement cycle.

observatoryObservations.label: Discovery of algorithms with automated evaluation
observatoryObservations.summary: The research team used Gemini models to propose algorithms, with automated evaluation of candidate solutions in mathematics and computing.
observatoryObservations.limitations: Experiments with a computable objective and human-chosen problems. Open-ended research and effects on successor generations require other evidence.

observatoryObservations.label: Unfamiliar visual reasoning puzzles
observatoryObservations.limitations: A verified result on one visual puzzle suite at a specified reasoning budget. It establishes neither broad competence nor performance on a later model.

observatoryObservations.label: Continuation of a supplied research-sabotage trajectory
observatoryObservations.summary: In a controlled evaluation the model continued a supplied sabotage attempt in 7% of cases. Researchers found no spontaneous sabotage in the unprompted tests.
observatoryObservations.limitations: The team tested with developer access. The seeded scenario and possible awareness of evaluation limit inference about real deployments or human intervention.

observatoryObservations.label: Worldwide growth in data-centre electricity demand
observatoryObservations.limitations: A global estimate for all data centres. Electricity use includes non-AI workloads and does not measure spare capacity.

observatoryObservations.label: Foundry manufacturing capacity
observatoryObservations.limitations: TSMC states that managed annual capacity exceeded this figure. It spans many chips and countries. AI accelerator availability also depends on packaging, memory and allocation.

observatoryObservations.label: Compute needed for a fixed language-model result
observatoryObservations.summary: The authors fit historical evaluations from 2012–2023 on two language-modeling benchmarks.
observatoryObservations.limitations: A retrospective estimate conditional on sample and benchmark. It cannot establish the rate on current research tasks.

observatoryObservations.label: Great Britain grid demand
observatoryObservations.publicationDateBasis: Operator timestamp for the data release
observatoryObservations.limitations: An observed half-hour of national demand. Spare power, data-centre outages and AI capacity require separate evidence.

observatoryObservations.label: ARC-AGI-3 at maximum reasoning · standard setup
observatoryObservations.limitations: One interactive reasoning suite. The configuration changes what information the model can carry between actions. Broad human-level ability requires additional independent tests.

observatoryObservations.label: ARC-AGI-3 at maximum reasoning · provider adapter
observatoryObservations.limitations: One interactive reasoning suite. The configuration changes what information the model can carry between actions. Broad human-level ability requires additional independent tests.

observatoryObservations.label: Coding performance after iterative changes to the agent
observatoryObservations.organization: Sakana AI and University of British Columbia
observatoryObservations.source: Sakana AI and University of British Columbia
observatoryObservations.limitations: The authors report a change from 20% to 50% on their coding test as agents edited their own software around a fixed foundation model. Independent replication and attribution for two specific links in a successor lineage remain open.

observatoryObservations.label: Previously open mathematics problems credited to AI alone
observatoryObservations.referenceDateBasis: Date the watch inspected the public problem register (New York)
observatoryObservations.limitations: Epoch credited five further solutions to joint human–AI work. The set is selected for mathematical interest and verifiability. Different systems and teams contributed. Attribution and the problem roster can change.

sources.title: AI Impacts · Survey of machine-learning researchers
sources.finding: The survey obtained 1,580 valid responses. Its combined forecasts put a 10% chance on machines doing every task better and more cheaply by 2027 and 50% by 2042. The halfway year was 2036 for doing research and writing a machine-learning conference paper, and 2052 for automating the occupation of AI researcher.
sources.limitation: Respondents answered subsets of questions and assumed no major disruption to science. Conditional on human-level machines, median respondents assigned 10% within two years and 60% within thirty years to vastly superhuman performance across professions. For a dramatic AI-driven acceleration of global technology, those figures were 20% and 80%. The Watch requires independent tests and evidence of a repeating causal loop.
sources.locator: Sections 2.3 and 3.2, Table 2, and Appendices E and F

sources.title: Forecasting Research Institute · Longitudinal Expert AI Panel, wave 8
sources.finding: The median expert gave an 80% chance of majority panel agreement on expert-level AGI before 2100. Given that recognition, the quarter, halfway and three-quarter dates were 2039, 2050 and 2065. A separate question on recognizing rapid progress gave 68% before 2100 and a conditional halfway year of 2045.
sources.limitation: The AGI question requires a commercial system that beats 90th-percentile professionals on at least 90% of nonphysical tasks in every primarily nonphysical occupation, at up to five times the equivalent labor cost. Its rapid-progress scenario also involves physical capabilities. Neither question stipulates the Watch’s testing or causal rules.

sources.title: Metaculus · When will a general AI system be publicly announced?
sources.finding: On November 24, the community forecast centered on 2030 for the first general AI system to be built, tested and publicly announced under the question’s rules.
sources.limitation: This crowd forecast can change as people update their predictions. Its public announcement date offers a comparison with the Watch’s estimate for independently demonstrated ability across domains. It has no weight in the Watch’s calculation.

sources.title: AI Futures Project · November timelines update
sources.finding: All six authors placed their halfway date for a superhuman AI researcher in 2027. Five placed the date for AI that outperforms top experts across virtually all cognitive tasks in 2028 and one in 2027.
sources.limitation: The authors assume no substantial deliberate slowdown and draw heavily on the same METR report about Anthropic. Their research milestone requires automated coding and experiment selection on par with the best human researcher. It can be reached before anyone independently verifies a repeating successor lineage.

sources.title: Forecasting Research Institute · Measuring a year of unusually fast gains
sources.finding: The researchers modeled a rise of at least 30 points in the best Epoch Capabilities Index score within twelve months. Their statistical model put its chance at 12% by the end of 2027 and 38% by the end of 2030.
sources.limitation: Under other plausible assumptions about volatility, their 2030 figure ranged from 7% to 59%. One year of gains on an index leaves the cause, persistence across generations and effect on technology beyond AI open.
sources.locator: Section 2.3 and its second endnote, November 2026 revision

sources.title: Forecasting Research Institute · Economic growth under rapid AI progress
sources.finding: Even assuming rapid AI progress, the expert panel’s median forecast for annual growth in advanced economies in 2050 was 5%, against a roughly 2% historical pace. The median among tournament forecasters was 3%.
sources.limitation: Economic output reflects financing, adoption, physical production and regional conditions. A jump in research capability can take years to reach these measures. GDP growth alone cannot identify a repeating improvement cycle or its cause.

sources.title: METR · AI research and development at Anthropic
sources.finding: At Anthropic, measured gains on the lab’s capability index came 1.9 times as fast after October 2025 as in the earlier period. The reported 95% interval was 1.5–2.8 times. METR judged that AI probably accounted for most of the recent acceleration.
sources.limitation: The attribution is a judgment under substantial uncertainty. Staff changes, compute, the choice of tasks and the earlier growth rate can also affect this one lab’s comparison.

sources.title: METR · Duration of AI tasks in the Q4 capability evaluation
sources.finding: Across two task suites, METR estimated that the human-expert working time corresponding to 50% AI success doubled every 3.61 months. The 95% interval on the doubling time was 2.08–4.94 months.
sources.limitation: These tasks emphasize software and research work. Longer tasks, higher reliability, transfer to unfamiliar domains and open-ended research each need their own measurements.

sources.title: Sakana AI and UBC · Darwin Gödel Machine
sources.finding: Researchers reported a coding agent that repeatedly edited agent code and tested successors. The resulting system’s SWE-bench score rose from 20% to 50%, with a separate coding benchmark improving from 14.2% to 30.7%.
sources.limitation: This developer experiment changed the software around a foundation model. A public, independently verified lineage would need to connect specific successive changes to the Watch’s required capability gains.

sources.title: Wang and colleagues · Testing self-improving coding agents
sources.finding: A second team reran the Darwin Gödel Machine method with different underlying models and a common starting agent. The starting agent solved 40% of a 60-task software test. Its selected successor scored 53.3%.
sources.limitation: This independently tests whether the method can discover better coding agents. The initial-to-final comparison does not identify how much each of two successive generations contributed on independent held-out tasks.

sources.title: ARC Prize · GPT-6.2 Astra on interactive reasoning tasks
sources.finding: On ARC-AGI-3, GPT-6.2 Astra at the same maximum reasoning setting scored 70.3% with the standard setup and 99.8% with the provider’s adapter, which retains the model’s internal reasoning state between requests.
sources.limitation: The tested setup matters even for the same model. The score describes a specific collection of interactive puzzles. Evidence from other domains and independent tests of transfer are still needed.

sources.title: Epoch AI · Attribution of solutions to open mathematics problems
sources.finding: Of 49 open mathematical challenges in the register on November 24, Epoch credited five solutions to AI alone and five to people working with AI. The distinction records who contributed the ideas behind each solution.
sources.limitation: A solution establishes a particular mathematical result. Judging broad superiority to leading experts requires repeatable comparisons across multiple disciplines.

sources.title: Epoch AI · Can AI automate Epoch?
sources.finding: Epoch gave six models tasks drawn from its own work. Stronger systems could suggest research directions but struggled to design experiments that would resolve the question or to catch flaws in their own experimental setup.
sources.limitation: The evaluators used one organization’s tasks and quality standards. The experiment identifies practical gaps without establishing a universal ceiling.

pace.validation: Within one published suite, keep the highest result in each measured release month at its actual release date.
